messages:
tara-docs: Quick sync — I opened a docs PR to consolidate our Dedicated -> Autoscale migration guidance (https://git.redwood/docs/pull/482). Need a few small but blocking pieces before I can merge:

- a compact k8s snippet showing how to label pods/tenants for ReservedPool -> AutoscalePolicy transition
- a short Terraform + Python SDK example for setting autoscale/burst settings
- wording tweak for the SLA section: clarify 'isolation' vs 'eviction' behavior when preemption happens

Can @sam-eng or @oliver-infra give the infra bits? @maria-ml might want to sanity-check the perf caveats. Jenna can you polish the SLA wording once we have the facts?

sam-eng: looking now. I can sketch the TF and Python snippets. do we want the TF to use module vars or a minimal inline resource?

tara-docs: minimal inline is better — readers come from the quickstart and shouldn't need module plumbing. 2-3 lines max to demonstrate API shape is fine.

oliver-infra: tagging in. For k8s labeling, we recommend using the tenant annotation + podPriority class. Example idiom we use in prod: annotate pods with `redwood/tenant-id` and `redwood/queue` so the autoscaler routes correctly. Also note: ReservedPool eviction happens at node allocator level; isolation guarantees are per-tenant label + reserved pool binding.

oliver-infra: quick k8s snippet (feel free to trim):

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: llm-worker
  labels:
    app: inference
  annotations:
    redwood/tenant-id: "tenant-42"
    redwood/queue: "dedicated"
spec:
  priorityClassName: redwood-dedicated
  containers:
  - name: worker
    image: redwood/llm-runtime:stable
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```

maria-ml: thanks — can we add a one-liner caveat about KV-cache warmup and model variant fallbacks when moving to Autoscale? some customers saw a 200-400ms cold-open regression that should be called out.

tara-docs: yes. suggestion for copy: "Note: autoscaling new instances may incur KV-cache warmup latency; we recommend conservative min-replicas or prewarm hooks for steady low-latency workloads." Jenna, feel free to rewrite.

sam-eng: TF snippet (minimal):

```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_autoscale_policy" "example" {
  tenant_id     = "tenant-42"
  min_replicas  = 1
  max_replicas  = 10
  cpu_target    = 70
  burst_policy {
    enabled = true
    burst_capacity = 2
  }
}
```

sam-eng: Python SDK example (very short):

```py
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
policy = client.create_autoscale_policy(tenant_id="tenant-42", min_replicas=1, max_replicas=10, cpu_target=70, burst_capacity=2)
print(policy.id)
```

jenna-techwriter: I can take the SLA paragraph. One question: do we call out "eviction" as a best-effort behavior or an SLA-exempt event? legal asked for explicit language around "unrecoverable preemption".

chris-sre: short answer — eviction due to capacity pressure is covered by our Dedicated SLA except when caused by customer config (e.g., tenant mislabeling) or forceful infra preemption (cloud maintenance/spot reclaim). We should list examples of SLA-exempt causes.

jenna-techwriter: ok I'll draft this: "Redwood Dedicated guarantees X availability within non-preemptive capacity. Evictions triggered by platform maintenance, third-party cloud preemption, or misconfiguration (missing tenant labeling) are exempt from uptime credits. Isolation guarantees apply only when a tenant is bound to a ReservedPool and resources remain within contracted limits." I'll post PR update.

tara-docs: perfect. two more tiny asks: 1) add a link to the SDK reference for create_autoscale_policy, and 2) fix a dead link in the top of the migration doc that points to the old terraform module (I left a TODO inline).

jenna-techwriter: I found the dead link — fixed in the branch. will add SDK ref link.

docs-bot: CI checks — spellcheck: passed, linkcheck: failed (1 broken link: /docs/old/dedicated-terraform)

tara-docs: thanks docs-bot — jenna already fixed that in branch, can we re-run linkcheck?

docs-bot: linkcheck re-run requested by tara-docs. queued.

maria-ml: one more perf note: in the examples, call out which model variants support kv-cache persistence across restarts. I'll send a short table to the PR comment.

sam-eng: uploaded a tiny patch to the PR with the TF + Python examples inline, and shortened the k8s snippet per tara's ask.

oliver-infra: quick FYI — we should avoid recommending priority classes that don't exist in OSS installs. add a comment that `redwood-dedicated` is created by our operator; otherwise use `high-priority`.

tara-docs: nice catch. jenna, could you add that as an OSS note?

jenna-techwriter: will do. I'll also add the SLA exemption bullet points and the prewarm recommendation. aim to push update within 90m.

sam-eng: LGTM on the edits so far. if nobody objects let's merge after jenna's wording and a green linkcheck.

chris-sre: no objections from SRE. thanks for being explicit on eviction causes.

tara-docs: thanks everyone — I'll merge once CI is green and the tiny OSS note + schema examples are in. :tada:
